description: OMP Desktop patch set for the pinned upstream OMP runtime: RPC host-tool scheduling and batch policy, settle-time run termination, and the all-toolCall batch count. Risk reduction only: it does NOT make the sole-batch contract strict — see status.

contract.invalidDeclaration: set_host_tools request is rejected; the value never degrades to the default
contract.invalidDeclarationDetail: RpcHostToolDefinition.concurrency/batchPolicy values outside their union throw in normalizeHostToolPolicy, which the set_host_tools command and the host-tool adapter both call

notes: This is an OMP Desktop-maintained patch level, not upstream OMP support: the runtime remains pinned at d49918f (omp/18.2.7) plus this patch set.
Rebuild the patch after any source edit with: git -C <checkout> diff > app/patches/oh-my-pi/0001-rpc-host-tool-transition-contract.patch, then refresh patch.sha256 and patch.bytes.

status.blocker: F3: a `kCursorExecResolved` sibling was executed by the provider/editor bridge before the assistant message existed, so its side effect cannot be prevented or retracted by any loop-level patch; PI counts every toolCall block, so the batch is still rejected, but "zero side effects in a rejected batch" is unreachable at this layer.
mitigationsApplied: batch admission counts every toolCall block of the assistant message (Cursor-resolved included), matching PI runtime.ts:2222
speculation is disabled for a provider call whose active tool set advertises a sole-declared tool, so no speculative physical work starts before the batch decision
